title: legal redlines scratchpad - contract clauses & talking points
content:
Quick scratchpad of clauses to watch and suggested negotiation posture. Mostly notes to myself - share with deal lead + legal if we want to take a hard line.

High-level goals: keep risk predictable, avoid open-ended obligations, preserve product IP and model/serving flexibility, be pragmatic on customer concerns re: data & outputs.

Priority items (check each deal):
- Liability cap: default = greater of $1,000,000 or 12 months of fees. Customer asking for unlimited/broad exception for IP/PD. Push back: offer carve-outs only for gross negligence/willful misconduct, not for ordinary contract claims. Consider: increase to 2x fees if strategic customer, otherwise keep standard.

- Indemnity: watch for customer indemnity that expands to cover provider for customer content (e.g., claims arising from use of the model on customer data). Our position: we indemnify for third-party claims alleging IP infringement by our services; customer indemnifies for their content and use of outputs that violate law. Avoid mutual full indemnities.

- Data usage & training: customers often want: "You may not use Customer Content to train models."
  - Our typical hosted stance: do not use Customer Content to improve models unless customer opts in. For dedicated/private we may need flexibility. Proposed clause: "Provider will not use Customer Content to train or improve models without Customer's prior written consent; aggregated/anonymized usage metrics may be used for service reliability and capacity planning."
  - TODO: confirm with infra whether anonymized telemetry is acceptable to customers (ENG-1825).

- IP / outputs: customers asking for ownership of Generated Output. Options:
  1) Grant customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free right to use Customer Data and the corresponding Outputs for their internal/business purposes.
  2) If customer demands full assignment: push back - offer license instead.
  - Note: make sure license includes right to sublicense to sub-agents (internal service stack).

- Confidentiality: standard NDA terms + carveouts for general feedback. Clarify retention & deletion obligations on termination. Customer may request proof of deletion; offer certificate of destruction after reasonable period.

- Security & compliance: expect ask for SOC2/ISO27001; provide certs if available and add standard security SLA. For regulated customers: add clause for data residency (EU-only), encryption-at-rest/in-transit, KMS support for private deployments.

- Breach notification: customer asks for 24 hours. Our posture: 72 hours with best-efforts interim notice. Push for 72 hours unless customer is highly regulated.

- Audit & inspection rights: limit to one remote audit per year, scope narrowly defined (security controls, not access to source code or model weights). Require NDA and reasonable notice (30 days). No on-site without mutual agreement.

- Subprocessors: require vendor transparency + ability to object to new subprocessors (limited window), but we cannot get customer approval on major cloud infra (AWS/GCP/Azure). Recommended: notice + list of approved subprocessors + right to object for sensitive data classes only.

- Export controls / sanctions: standard termination & compliance language; customer may ask for representation that we won't serve sanctioned users. Keep standard language and right to suspend for sanctioned activity.

- SLA / uptime & credits: typical ask = financial credits + termination right if repeated downtime. Our standard: 99.9% monthly uptime for hosted API, credits formula in schedule. Avoid automatic termination for brief SLO misses - require material breach standard (e.g., repeated misses in 3-month window). For Dedicated: different SLOs depending on committed capacity.

- Term & termination: retention of data on termination - offer 30 days to export followed by deletion unless otherwise agreed. For long-term contracts, negotiate exit support separately.

- Limitation of remedies: prefer monetary damages only; exclude injunctive relief unless specifically required for IP theft. Customer may push for broader remedies - escalate to legal if so.

Negotiation talking points (for AE/PS to use in calls):
- "We're happy to negotiate practical safeguards on data - we won't use your customer content to train models without consent; we do use aggregate telemetry for reliability. If you need stricter controls, our Private deployment option supports that."
- "Our liability cap is designed to align with the commercial economics of the relationship. For strategic enterprise deals we can consider tailored caps tied to committed spend."
- "Audit requests are reasonable; we prefer remote, scoped audits to avoid operational disruption. We'll provide SOC2 reports and supporting evidence."
- "If IP ownership of Outputs is critical, we can grant a broad, perpetual license. Full assignment is uncommon for model outputs - let's discuss why you need assignment vs. license."

Quick clause language snippets (draft-friendly):
- Data usage: "Provider will not use Customer Content to train, finetune, or improve any models or models' parameters without Customer's prior written consent. Provider may use anonymized and aggregated telemetry solely to operate and improve service reliability."
- Liability cap: "Except for liability arising from (i) willful misconduct or gross negligence, or (ii) Provider's breach of confidentiality obligations, Provider's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (A) $1,000,000 and (B) the amounts paid by Customer to Provider in the 12 months preceding the claim."
- Breach notice: "Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to notify Customer of any confirmed security incident affecting Customer Data no later than seventy-two (72) hours after discovery. Provider will provide updates as material information becomes available."

Open items / TODOs: 
- Confirm with infra/security whether 72 hr breach window is acceptable or we need 7 days for certain incidents. (Ping: Liam Brown in SRE).
- Check with Product on telemetry usage (what fields are collected, can we limit PII?). (ENG-3052).
- Compile recent SOC2 package and upload to Sales Portal (Sales ask: ACCOUNT-998).
- For customer X (CON-245): they insist on assignment of Outputs + 24hr breach notice - escalate to Head of Legal for one-off terms.

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight, route finalized language into contracts repo (contracts/templates) after deal closes. Save standard alternative language versions (cap increases, shorter breach windows) in templates.

References: Confluence standard SaaS agreement (linked above), previous redline examples in GitHub PR #87.

End of scratchpad.
